name: Hypereosinophilic Syndrome

criteria.description: Persistent eosinophilia >1.5 x 10^9/L for more than 6 months
Evidence of organ involvement or dysfunction attributable to eosinophilia
Exclusion of secondary causes of eosinophilia such as parasitic infection, allergies, or malignancies
Bone marrow biopsy showing eosinophilic proliferation without evidence of other hematologic malignancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Persistent eosinophilia >1.5 x 10^9/L for >6 months, evidence of organ damage due to eosinophilia, and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of secondary eosinophilia and other myeloproliferative disorders.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic cardiac involvement leading to restrictive cardiomyopathy

occasional.notes: Due to hypercoagulable state from eosinophil-mediated endothelial damage

rare.notes: Due to embolic events from cardiac involvement

laboratory: Elevated serum vitamin B12 and tryptase in some cases
imaging: Echocardiogram showing endomyocardial fibrosis or thrombus
Chest CT showing pulmonary infiltrates or fibrosis
MRI brain in cases with neurological symptoms
genetic: FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene in a subset of patients
Other myeloproliferative neoplasm-associated mutations may be present
other: Tissue biopsy showing eosinophilic infiltration and organ damage

distinguishingFeatures: Clonal eosinophilic proliferation with abnormal cytogenetics
Presence of blasts in peripheral blood or bone marrow
Identification of parasitic organisms or ova in stool or tissue
History of atopy or allergic disease

references: Chusid MJ, Dale DC, West BC, Wolff SM. The hypereosinophilic syndrome: analysis of fourteen cases with review of the literature. Medicine (Baltimore). 1975 Jul;54(1):1-27.
Gotlib J. World Health Organization-defined eosinophilic disorders: 2017 update on diagnosis, risk stratification, and management. Am J Hematol. 2017 Nov;92(11):1243-1259.
Simon HU, Rothenberg ME, Bochner BS, et al. Refining the definition of hypereosinophilic syndrome. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2010 Jan;126(1):45-49.
